analysis: Both units are CHANGELOG.md head_text excerpts (lines 1450-1900), i.e. documentation of historical release notes with no executable code or config. The file_changes patch shows the changed range is the top of the file (head lines 11-100, a new v0.10.1 candidate section). The supplied units cover older release history, which is unchanged context. I examined the text against the threat model, notably T-041/SEC-035. The changelog records the SSD prefix-cache TTL raise from 15 to 30 min as the SEC-035 re-acceptance, which matches the canonical T-041 text (30-minute TTL, env can only shorten) and is therefore not a new divergence. The notes on epoch retention across eviction/expiry are consistent with T-041's statement that the epoch is a routing-evidence generation and not a purge primitive. Other security-relevant claims are descriptive only: removal of the unauthenticated /v1/provider/earnings lookup (T-031), fail-closed attestation challenges, App Attest protocol 3 only, the registration timestamp freshness requirement, and the minimum provider version floor. These tighten controls and do not weaken any threat-model mitigation. Changelog statements are not proof of the implementing code. Remaining integration questions: the v0.10.1 section (head lines 11-100, outside the supplied units) lists page-cache accounting changes that may affect memory admission (T-016/T-029 availability) and GLM logprob refusal relying on a coordinator in another repo. Those need review in the source files that implement them, not in this changelog. No regression is identifiable from the supplied units.
